name: hobb

extraAngles.prompt: TRANSLATORS AS CLOSE READERS of Robin Hobb's sentence — the richest untouched angle. FETCH FIRST: Arnaud Mousnier-Lompré (French translator of L'Assassin royal) — his interviews at ActuSF and Elbakin.net on rendering Hobb's sentence, tense and register; the Dutch translators Feberwee and Cuijpers as named in the Duits thesis; Tkach 2021, Naukovyi visnyk MHU 52(2) 182–185 (translating the Elderlings' names); the UNIGE names thesis (Jeanneret) — the PDF sits on archive-ouverte.unige.ch behind the landing page the first sweep fetched; Chandarana & Choudhary, 'Tolkienian Tools … Farseer' (Towards Excellence 14.2) — read the paper, not its landing page. The claims worth most say what a translator had to DO to a Hobb sentence (length, clause order, the first-person hedge, the plain noun) and why.

CLAIM WHAT IS ALREADY FETCHED, then take the second routes. ON DISK under prose-research/hobb-raw/ (read the file, claim it, log it in sourcesRead): 5000words.txt (Hobb, '5000 Words About Myself', Finncon 2004 — 'Something about the style does not lend itself to shorter tales'; a completely different sort of voice), interzone98.txt (Interzone 98, Aug 1995, the ONLY contemporary reception of the prose and it DISSENTS: 'Stylistically, the novel is patchy'; identify the reviewer), asimovs9702.txt (Asimov's Feb 1997 'On Books'), tor2014review.txt (Justin Landon, Tor.com 2014: 'without question, a slow novel'; the second first-person voice), sh-liveship.txt (Stephanie Dray, Strange Horizons 2001: pacing the most frequent complaint), guardian2017.txt (Alison Flood interview: Lindholm 'a little more snarky … less emotional'; the Fool had one sentence in the outline), independent2015.txt, orullian.txt (Peter Orullian interview: 'I slow down and put in the small details'), guardian2014.txt; hobb-acad/assistant.txt (Hodunok 2024). THEN the second routes: Mendlesohn, Rhetorics of Fantasy (2008) p. 16 via archive.org search-inside on item rhetoricsoffanta0000mend (no borrow needed for snippets); Mandala, Language in Science Fiction and Fantasy (2010) pp. 100–130 via archive.org search-inside or Bloomsbury Collections; Oliver, Magic Words, Magic Worlds (McFarland 2022) epigraph chapter via Google Books web preview; Ekman, Here Be Dragons (2013); Borowska-Szerszun, Extrapolation 60.1 (2019) doi 10.3828/extr.2019.2 via OpenAlex oa_url / Unpaywall / ResearchGate / the UwB repository search; Shropshire 2019 (Oklahoma State MS on geographic realism — the only work on Hobb's PLACE description) via the OSU catalogue or ProQuest; the r/Fantasy AMAs (2012, 2014, 2017) via Wayback id_ captures of old.reddit URLs found through the CDX API; two or three video-essay transcripts via youtube-transcript-api or an Invidious captions endpoint ('Robin Hobb prose', 'Assassin's Apprentice analysis', 'Fitz narration').

the well-known critics ABSENT from the first sweep, by name + 'Hobb': Amal El-Mohtar (New York Times, Assassin's Fate, 2017); Liz Bourke (Tor.com / Locus reviews of Fool's Quest and Assassin's Fate); Gary K. Wolfe (Locus); Niall Alexander (Tor.com); Jo Walton on the Farseer books (the captured Walton piece is on Lindholm's Wizard of the Pigeons — find the Farseer one); the Clute & Grant Encyclopedia of Fantasy (1997) entry (SFE is cited, EoF is not); Locus interview excerpts 2014 onward; Hobb's essay in Meditations on Middle-earth (2001, ed. Haber) — her own words on influence; podcasts with transcripts (Coode Street, Sword & Laser, Fantasy Faction). Praise and dissent equally; a sentence about her SENTENCES outweighs a verdict on the books.

THE EPIGRAPH CENSUS (the cheapest second source for the section's part A, which rests on one article): Elliott's reread series — 539 entries, every one fetched raw at HTTP 200 and on disk under prose-research/hobb-raw/ (find them by grep for 'Elliott' in the state's sourcesRead and the raw dir) — records what each chapter's opening document IS. Tally, chapter by chapter across the Farseer/Tawny Man/Fitz and the Fool books: the document KIND of each epigraph (treatise, letter, scroll, song, annal, recipe …), its length band, its stance (impersonal record vs personal), and the few Oliver calls 'infected' by the narrator's voice. Write the tally as claims with the entry URL as source and a ≤12-word quote of the epigraph's opening where one is on the page. This grounds rules 2, 4, 21 and 27 in a count rather than one metaphor.

[146]: the page is Spanish — an English rendering cannot be VERIFIED_VERBATIM → VERIFIED_SUBSTANCE with the Spanish located. [221]–[223] (rpgstorytellers.com): the state roster marks the source substantive:false, 'reads as AI-generated' → NOT_FOUND for the section's purposes (note the roster's own verdict). [150]: scoped on the page to SHORT STORIES ('In a short story, I'm the opposite…'; the same interview's 'In a novel, I sprawl' is partial row 20) → PARTIAL naming the scope limb; rule 18 must not generalise it. The 39 cross-angle near-duplicate pairs (e.g. [0]/[160], [78]/[224], [205]/[380], [255]/[369]): keep the earlier index and mark the later PARTIAL 'duplicate of #N'. The chair re-take file verdicts-hobb-retake-r6.json already restored trueWording := quote for [137]–[144], [147]–[149], [300]–[314]; do not undo it. Every trueWording you write is at most twelve words; 178 kept rows exceed twelve — note 'fullSentence: trim before any copy' on each you touch.
synthNotes: Say in one sentence that section A rests on ONE article (Oliver, 40 of 346 rows, the only peer-reviewed style criticism; the rest is student theses, relays, one-passage uses and corpus papers that measure nothing about her prose). Count DISTINCT source documents one way (Mendlesohn-via-Oliver is one; two annotations on one Fedwren page are one; three Vacuous Wastrel posts are one). Rewrite rule 5 (the Duits 'disagreement' is two registers) and rule 18 (short stories only; rule 17 binds the dossier) to their pages; fix rule 8's arithmetic ('ten' lists twelve) and the file counts (27 verdict files; 106 distinct URLs, 88 substantive); list the eleven blocked/unreached sources in the coverage table so the zeroes stop reading as clean. Rules whose evidence is not prose evidence — 12 (worldbuilding advice), 31 (the private glossary; Mead paraphrases Hobb's post: SINGLE SOURCE in substance), 6's 'an office may replace a name' (a plot fact), 27 (one metaphor in one epigraph), 28 ('institutions as procedure, one clause each' — no source says it) — are parked on the DM page or rewritten to what the sources say. If the epigraph census landed, part A's rules 2, 4, 21, 27 cite its counts first. If the translators angle landed, give its sentence-level findings their own numbered features. The Interzone 98 dissent and Landon's 'slow novel' go into the reception paragraph as the contemporary record. The DM page cites book, chapter and page; never copy a trueWording over twelve words (178 kept rows are flagged fullSentence).
